resource_model.principle: Persistent observations are priors; current qstat/probes decide present scheduling.
resource_model.probe_role: current-session evidence when large batches or ambiguous live pressure make priors insufficient
do_not_infer: A previously fast queue will remain fastest in future sessions.
A previously backlogged queue is permanently bad.
A successful probe is an availability guarantee beyond the current scheduling window.

submission_invariants: Commit local changes before remote PBS submission.
Push the target branch before cluster submission.
Fast-forward the target cluster worktree only before submission, never while pinned jobs are running.
Verify branch, commit, clean status, and qsub before submitting.
Repair failed chunks by cancel/resubmit/rebuild-merge, not qmove.

excluded_by_default.C24: Manual node range starts at 17 nodes; M6 chunks are one-node jobs.
excluded_by_default.C36: Manual node range starts at 25 nodes; M6 chunks are one-node jobs.
excluded_by_default.C12-LONG2: Observed stopped in live queue state; keep out of automatic scheduling.
excluded_by_default.C17: Conditional only: cnode37 passed 8-core Stephanov probes, but cnode38/cnode39 lack git and current PBS git guard exits 127; use only with known-good placement or a gitless guard.
excluded_by_default.C17-LONG: Conditional only: cnode37 passed 8-core Stephanov probes, but cnode38/cnode39 lack git and current PBS git guard exits 127; use only with known-good placement or a gitless guard.
excluded_by_default.G: GPU queue reserves GPU resources by default; not for CPU-only TLTM chunks.
excluded_by_default.G-LONG: GPU queue reserves GPU resources by default; not for CPU-only TLTM chunks.
excluded_by_default.G-A100: GPU queue reserves GPU resources by default; not for CPU-only TLTM chunks.

scoring_rules: Reject queues outside manual node/core/walltime limits.
Reject disabled or stopped queues from live qstat -Qf.
Penalize queued, waiting, and held backlog.
Penalize queues already assigned many chunks in the current launch.
Prefer short CPU queues before long queues when comparable.
Treat observed successes as compatibility priors, not as fixed availability guarantees.
Use fresh qstat snapshots and production-shape probes for large or ambiguous batches.
Record queue plan and observations for future reuse.
